Two years without a word, Ana. So, tell me honestly: was it the right decision?
On the whole, yes. It took me a long time to settle in, but I would not go back now.
I did the opposite, you know. I sold the workshop in March and I moved back to Sao Paulo.
You sold the workshop? You had that place for twenty years.
I know. I was worn out. I was working every weekend and I was still only getting by. I needed a fresh start.
And now? Do you look forward to Monday morning?
Honestly, yes. It is noisy and it is expensive, but I have found something I can stick with. And my son lives ten minutes away.
Then it was worth it. We took stock at the same time and we walked in opposite directions.
I have been working on this house for years.

I get by on a lot less than I did in the city.
On the whole, it was the best decision I ever made.

People keep asking me whether I regret it, and the honest answer is no, not for a single day. I took stock last January, the way I always do. Nine years ago I did not know what I wanted. I was worn out, I was working every weekend, and I was getting by, but nothing more than that. Now the mornings belong to me. The work on the house is slow, but it is steady, and every room that is finished belongs to me in a way that nothing in the city ever did. I do not have a plan for next year. I have a list, and I stick with it, one line at a time. On the whole, I sleep better.

Everyone talks about the fresh start. Nobody warns you about the first winter. I moved out here in March, and by August I was seriously thinking about going back. The house was cold, the internet was terrible, and I did not know a single person in the town. It took me three years to settle in, not one. What changed things was the workshop. I started fixing chairs for the neighbors, badly at first, and I stuck with it. Now I have more work than I can handle, and I unwind in the evening by doing exactly the thing I do all day. My advice for anyone planning the same move is simple: give it three years, not one.
